items.title: LTX 2.5 raises the bar for video models
items.oneliner: LTX 2.5 ships open weights for video generation, pushing faster, higher-quality outputs into developers' hands instead of closed demos.

items.title: Nvidia shipped Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
items.oneliner: Nvidia's 30B Nemotron 3.5 Lightning targets long-running agents, signaling specialized smaller models are beating brute-force generalists.

items.title: Tencent showed agentic 3D world generation
items.oneliner: WorldClaw turns open-ended prompts into explorable 3D worlds, hinting that game prototyping is becoming an agent workflow.

items.title: Anthropic is watermarking Claude outputs
items.oneliner: Anthropic is adding hidden markers to Claude text, code, and files, making provenance a product feature before regulators force it.

items.title: Deadbugz weaponizes the MCP ecosystem
items.oneliner: Deadbugz hid credential-stealing prompts in MCP servers after three interactions, proving agent supply chains are already an attack surface.

items.title: Hidden reasoning is no longer hidden
items.oneliner: Researchers extracted hidden reasoning and recovered 367 personal data fragments and 182 credentials from public traces.

items.title: England's courts banned Meta smart glasses
items.oneliner: England and Wales banned Meta smart glasses in courts, showing wearable AI is now triggering real institutional pushback.

items.title: Signal automated key verification
items.oneliner: Signal shipped automatic key verification, bringing key transparency to normal users instead of leaving serious security to power users.

items.title: Nvidia is financing the compute buildout
items.oneliner: Nvidia and finance giants are mobilizing $500 billion for AI infrastructure, which tells you demand is now a capital markets story.

items.title: Anthropic signed a massive compute deal
items.oneliner: Anthropic's reported $9.1 billion Riot compute deal makes clear frontier labs are locking in power before capacity tightens further.
